Write the complex number $z$, shown on the Argand diagram above, in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ giving $\theta $ in radians to $3$ decimal places.

feedback.problem: Write the complex number $z=1-\text{i}\sqrt{3}$ in exponential form.
feedback.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\sqrt{3})| \\  & =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{3}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2$ and $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{3}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=2\,{\text{e}}^{5\pi \text{i}/3}.
$$
